newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mostly off after wide price swings.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mostly off after wide price swings.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended mostly lower with rising concern over increasing lumber supplies in the spring weighing on back months, traders said.

Futures showed wide price swings during the day with carryover demand from two consecutive limit advances lifting January and March to new contract highs again before general profit taking took all months lower. Nearbys again found support late on firmer cash markets but deferred months remained pressured from later supply concerns, they said.
January set a new high of $398.80 and March of $395.80 per tbf before falling.
A new Canadian yearly quota will be in effect by late spring and there will be more lumber coming into the U.S. from Canada by then. Tight supplies currently kept nearbys supported, traders said.
Futures had a $15.00 trading limit Tuesday following the two days of limit advances, but limits will return to $10.00 per tbf Wednesday as November only closed slightly higher.
Lumber closed $3.00 per tbf higher to $6.90 lower with November up most at $388.70 and January up $0.50 at $395.00. May paced the setback in deferreds.
